penetration_assumption: Composite of six separately-stated assumptions, each anchored to a line ARY already runs rather than to a generic percentage. (1) OTC oral therapeutics ₹22,000: 1 in 20 of 4,700 residents buys one ulcer-gel tube or gargle bottle a year at ~₹110 — cross-checked against ARY's own Antiseptic Lotion subgroup (₹29,394/yr on 4 selling SKUs = ₹7,349/SKU) and Pain Relief (₹44,351 on 13 = ₹3,412/SKU), then discounted for the free 100-bed Akal Charitable Hospital OPD on campus. (2) Herbal mouthwash ₹5,000: one new proposition earns what an existing live mouthwash SKU earns — ₹23,325 / 4 live SKUs = ₹5,831/SKU/yr — ~85% incremental. (3) Floss + floss picks ₹10,000: 3% of ARY's ~1,400 adults (1,102 Eternal University students + 145 faculty/staff + a slice of staff families) floss, 2 packs/yr at ~₹90. (4) Tooth powder ₹12,000: 1 in 25 of the ~1,900 adults over 35 (staff families + the 487 AIRWE rural women) buys a 100g dant manjan four times a year at ₹55. (5) Denture care ₹10,000: ~25 denture wearers on campus (200-300 residents aged 60+ x ~10% India denture-wearing prevalence at 60+), ~₹400/wearer/yr actually spent at ARY. (6) Ortho wax + interdental ₹8,000: 0.5% of ~2,400 school and university students in braces — deliberately below the urban 1.5% because the nearest orthodontist is Solan/Nahan, not Baru Sahib — at ~₹690/yr each. Every penetration rate above is ESTIMATED by me; none is measured. The revenue total is therefore the weakest number in this analysis, while the verdict itself rests on VERIFIED queries.
probe_evidence:
Live SQL over FR8HODBNEW, window 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31 (DB current to 2026-08-30 20:30). I drove everything from direct SQL rather than `ary assort probe` because probe returned different results for identical terms across runs in this session (`clove laung` gave 0 SKUs on one invocation and 3 on the next) and any term containing a hyphen silently zeroes the whole query.

CATEGORY SHAPE (VERIFIED): oral care = subgroups 807 Tooth Paste (194), 803 Tooth Brush (107), 607 Mouth Wash (12), 804 Tooth Pick (4), 876 Tongue Cleaner (2), 808 Toothpest Inactive (1), plus 3 misfiled SKUs found by name search (Colgate Brush 22/- Super Shine and Colgate Brush Junior filed under House Hold/Brush; Dabur Meswak 100G filed under Spices/Spices Paste). Total 323 listed SKUs, 117 sold in 12 months, 206 sold nothing, and NOT ONE of the 206 has any stock on hand. Sales ₹7,61,414 = 0.99% of ARY's ₹7,66,83,492 and ₹162/resident/yr. A wider name sweep (colgate, pepsodent, closeup, sensodyne, dabur, dant, manjan, listerine, plax, floss, tongue, datun, miswak, oral-b, tooth, denture, gum paint) found 342 SKUs but the extra 19 were substring garbage — Bluetooth Buds/Headset/Speaker (contain "tooth"), 8 Kandy Floss garments (contain "floss"), Odonil Room Spray Floral Bliss (contains "oral b"), Patanjali Peedantak pain balm (contains "dant").

PROVENANCE OF THE DEAD TAIL (VERIFIED, the decisive query): of the 203 strict-subgroup SKUs with zero 12-month sales, 140 have NEVER been purchased once in the entire PurchaseHeader/PurchaseDetail ledger, 139 have NEVER sold in the whole sales history, and 38 more were last purchased before 2024-09-01. So 178 of 203 are phantom catalogue rows or two-years-abandoned, all at zero stock.

AVAILABILITY (VERIFIED): 65 of the 117 selling SKUs (56%) are at zero on-hand as of 2026-08-30; those 65 earned ₹2,56,064 — 34% of the category — while they were available; mean 158.8 days since last sale. There were 354 trading days in the window, yet the #1 oral-care SKU (Sensodyne Sensitive Tooth Brush, ₹54,484) sold on only 233 of them, and the average selling SKU on 52.6. Concrete stockouts: Close Up 80 G last sold 2026-05-13 (₹12,240, on-hand 0); Closeup Everfresh+ 150Gm last sold 2026-05-23 (₹13,681, on-hand 0); Sensodyne 40+10 Gm Fresh Mint last sold 2026-03-07 (₹13,680, on-hand 0); Colgate Visible White 120 Gm last sold 2026-07-08 (₹11,020, on-hand 0); Dabur Red Paste 80 Gm last sold 2026-05-31 (₹9,840, on-hand 0). Mouthwash: 10 of 12 SKUs at zero stock, including Colgate Plax 250 Ml.

GENUINELY ABSENT — zero SKUs, each checked with several vocabularies: floss/floss picks/irrigator 0 (excluding Kandy Floss garments); denture ANYTHING 0 (denture, dentur, fixon, fittydent, poligrip, polident, dentofix, clinsodent, val clean); chlorhexidine + povidone gargle 0 (hexidine, clohex, rexidin, betadine, povidone, gargle, zaigargle); mouth-ulcer gel 0 (zytee, dologel, mucopain, orasore, hexigel, ulcer, oral gel, mouth ulcer); herbal mouthwash 0; interdental/ortho oral care 0 — the 4 hits on "ortho" are Zandu Ortho Vedic Oil, 2x Dr Ortho Pain Relief Oil and Moov Ortho Gel, all pain relief; electric brush + replacement heads 0 (electric tooth, electric brush, brush head, sonicare, proclinical — the diff's "15 SKUs on electric" and "27 on power" resolve to Panasonic cells, Milton Kool Sonic bottles and Bluetooth Buds); datun/miswak/peelu sticks 0; gum paint + oil pulling + sensoform + amdent 0; whitening strips/pen 0; mukhwas/mouth freshener 0.

LISTED BUT DORMANT: tooth powder is the clean case — exactly 2 SKUs exist (0333 Patanjali Dant Manjan 100 Gm, 09F6 Patanjali Dant Manjan 100 Gm Advanced), both zero 12-month sales AND zero on-hand, so "never sold" here proves nothing about demand; it proves they were never stocked.

MARGIN (VERIFIED from the purchase ledger, not the price master): PurchaseDetail carries IncludeInRate=false (PurchaseCost is ex-GST, 5% added) while SaleDetail carries IncludeInRate=true (FinalSaleAmount is GST-inclusive) — mixing them yields a false 24.95%. Put on a common ex-GST footing across 108 SKUs covering 98% of category sales: oral care 17.64% overall; Tooth Paste 10.05%, Tooth Brush 35.23%, Mouth Wash 13.08%, Tongue Cleaner 44.39%, Tooth Pick 43.99%; group-level Medicare 21.83%, Personal Care 17.95%, Toiletories 16.04%.

WHY THIS IS NOT A DEMAND PROBLEM: the category grew +10.7% YoY (₹6,87,881 in Sep-24..Aug-25 to ₹7,61,553) while the count of SKUs selling per month rose from ~43 to ~53. Toothpaste moves 23.7 units per trading day in term months and 15.1 in the winter shutdown — the term calendar, not the SKU count, drives it, so substitution inside toothpaste is nearly complete. I therefore did NOT quote the naive ₹12,84,176 "forgone at own rate" that the stockout arithmetic produces; most of it is absorbed by a sibling SKU. 1.75 toothpaste tubes per resident per year is roughly the Indian per-capita norm.
kill_reason: Not a kill — the absent lines are real — but the ADD recommendation is close to worthless against the availability finding, and that has to be said plainly. The whole genuinely-missing set is worth ~₹67,000/yr revenue and ~₹16,000/yr gross profit: 8.8% of a ₹7.61 lakh category and 0.09% of ARY's ₹7.67 Cr business. In the same category, 65 of the 117 SKUs that demonstrably sell are at zero stock today, holding ₹2,56,064 of proven annual demand, and 140 of the 206 dead SKUs have never been purchased once. Adding 13 rows to a catalogue that already carries 140 rows nobody ever bought is the exact error the central finding warns against. Separately, the coverage diff that triggered this task is unreliable in BOTH directions and should be corrected in the corpus: its single must-have "missing" (denture cleansing tablets) is real but is the smallest and least certain line here, while its "covered" verdicts include denture adhesive matched to Fevicol, water flosser matched on "power", electric toothbrush matched to Panasonic cells and Milton bottles, tongue cleaner matched to steel utensils, and mouth-ulcer gel matched to "Odonil Floral Bliss" and "Kandy Floss". Its own alcohol-free-mouthwash line is already covered by Colgate Plax 250 Ml (0G4P) — listed, selling, and currently out of stock.
top_skus: Zytee RB Gel 10g (mouth ulcer) — highest-frequency absent line, fits ARY's existing Medicare shelf
Dabur Lal Dant Manjan 100g — replaces the 2 dead Patanjali manjan SKUs that were never stocked
Himalaya Active Fresh mouthwash 215ml (herbal — the only genuinely new mouthwash proposition; Colgate Plax already covers alcohol-free)
Oral-B / Colgate ZigZag waxed dental floss 25-50m
3-in-1 floss picks 100pc (~₹66, carries the 44% toothpick/tongue-cleaner margin)
STIM Ex orthodontic relief wax strips
Smyle or Dologel CT oral gel (second ulcer SKU)
blockers: SEQUENCING — the real blocker. 65 of 117 selling oral SKUs are at zero stock right now and 140 of the 206 dead SKUs were never purchased once. Shelf and working capital spent on 13 new lines before the reorder discipline is fixed will simply create 13 more phantom rows. Fix availability on the existing 117 first; this add-list is a phase-2 item.

SUPPLIER REACH FROM RAJGARH HP — specialty dental (ICPA Proxa, STIM ortho wax, Fittydent, Val-Clean) has no rural-HP FMCG distribution; these are pharma-wholesale or e-commerce lines. Sourcing them means a Solan/Chandigarh pharma wholesaler relationship, not the existing distributor route. NOT-CHECKED: I did not query ARY's supplier master to see which distributors actually service Baru Sahib, so the sourcing cost and MOQ are unknown.

FREE CAMPUS HOSPITAL SUPPRESSES OTC DEMAND — Akal Charitable Hospital (100 beds, 11 doctors, ~120-131 free outside OPD patients/day) treats residents at no cost, which is why the ulcer-gel and gargle estimate was cut. ARY still sells ₹3.13 lakh of Medicare so the effect is partial, not total.

ELDERLY COHORT IS TINY — Baru Sahib is a school and university township (Akal Academy ~1,250, Eternal University 1,102, School of Spiritual Sciences 305, AIRWE 487 rural women, staff families ~850-1,450). Denture care serves maybe 25 people. It is the diff's one flagged must-have and the least defensible line in this list.

ORTHODONTIC BASE UNPROVEN — braces need an orthodontist and the nearest is Solan/Nahan, so the 0.5% prevalence I used is a guess a third of the urban rate. If nobody on campus is in braces the ortho wax and interdental lines are zero, not ₹8,000.

WINTER SHUTDOWN — the permanent resident base drops to ~1,700-2,300 for ~23 days from ~29 Dec to ~20 Jan (measured three times on ARY's own till). Slow-moving new lines bought in December sit unsold for a month.

NO LICENCE OR COLD-CHAIN BLOCKER — every proposed SKU is OTC or cosmetic and needs no refrigeration. MEDIUM confidence: I did not verify ARY's drug-licence status, but they already sell paracetamol, cough syrup, Benadryl and antiseptic lotion, so whatever permission covers that shelf covers this one.

CORPUS DEFECT — assort/research/coverage/oralcare.json must be corrected before anyone buys against it; its broad-match verdicts are substring artefacts (Fevicol as denture adhesive, Panasonic cells as electric toothbrushes, steel utensils as tongue cleaners). Also: `ary assort probe` gave non-reproducible results for identical terms in this session and silently returns zero when any term contains a hyphen — that tool needs a fix before it is trusted as the anti-false-gap guard the vault says it is.
